name: GGUF IQ4_XS (non-linear 4-bit, 256-value super-block with 6-bit sub-block scales)
bits: 4.4597 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '4.25 bpw non-linear quantization'. block_iq4_xs = { ggml_half d; uint16_t scales_h; uint8_t scales_l[QK_K/64]; uint8_t qs[QK_K/2]; } = 2 + 2 + 4 + 128 = 136 bytes / 256 = 4.25 bpw
quality_delta: Official tool string '4.25 bpw non-linear quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 perplexity delta published in any primary source found. Null + note.
notes: SCHEMA MISMATCH: there is no ggml/iq* value in the quantization scheme enum, so this record uses the closest existing value 'gguf-q4_k_m' (or 'gguf-q2_k') and puts the true type in `name` and `bits`. Requested enum additions are listed in the task report. Weight-only by construction: activations are promoted to q8_K (an intermediate dot-product format, not a storage format) and the matmul runs at fp16/bf16, so native_support is deliberately EMPTY and the whole accelerator ecosystem is emulated_support. No accelerator has an i-quant or k-quant path in silicon. COMMON TO ALL IQ-QUANTS, verified from ggml/src/ggml-common.h: they use the QK_K = 256 super-block like the K-quants, but instead of a UNIFORM integer grid they quantize to indices into a per-block CODEBOOK of 256 learned non-uniform 4-bit values (the 'i' in i-quant is for the codebook grid / i-quant from the ik_llama.cpp lineage). The index lookup is table-driven at dequant time, which is why they compress better than K-quants at the same nominal bits and why they dequantize more slowly - the dot product needs a gather from the codebook. This is a real throughput trade, not a free win. BACKEND SITUATION, verified: the CUDA library shipped in llamafile releases is size-optimized and OMITS the IQ-quant kernels (IQ1_*, IQ2_*, IQ3_*, IQ4_*); offloading an IQ-quantized model to an NVIDIA GPU therefore leaves those layers on the CPU with correct output but no GPU acceleration (qlab2-llamafile-support-docs). The Metal and ROCm builds are NOT size-optimized and include full IQ-quant GPU support - so an RX 7900 XTX on ROCm/HIP is in a materially better IQ position than an RTX 4090 on a stock llamafile build. Vulkan has no dedicated IQ-quant path. Upstream llama.cpp has per-type dequant kernels; ik_llama.cpp additionally ships the Trellis family (IQ1_KT/IQ2_KT/IQ3_KT/IQ4_KT, integer-base trellis, CUDA PR 113 / Metal PR 475 / NEON PR 471 / CPU PR 441) and _R4/_R16 row-interleaved variants. IQ4_XS is the one i-quant that is structurally a K-quant: it uses the full QK_K = 256 super-block, uniform 4-bit codebook indices in qs[QK_K/2] (128 bytes), and a TWO-LEVEL scale - a single fp16 d plus a packed 6-bit scale per 32-element sub-block stored as scales_l[QK_K/64] (4 bytes, low bits) and scales_h (uint16_t, the high bits of all 8 sub-blocks at once). That packing is why it reaches 4.25 bpw rather than the 4.5 bpw that a flat fp16-per-32-scale layout would cost, and it is the closest analogue in the i-quant family to the q4_K design. MIXTURE: base iq4_xs, promoted to Q5_K in the first n_layer/8 ffn_down layers only when no imatrix is present (same !has_imatrix guard as IQ4_NL), attn_v -> Q5_K when n_gqa >= 4, Q8_0 on 8-expert models, and Q5_K on attn_output for Mixtral. On the 70B path attn_v q3_K/q4_K -> Q5_K. The official string says 4.25 bpw but the measured whole-model figure is 4.4597 - the gap is the promoted tensors plus embeddings/output that stay wider. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'gguf-q4_k_m' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'gguf-iq4-xs'.
